articles.title: Hansi Flick: "Nuestra reacción tras las derrotas ha sido buena"
articles.standfirst: El técnico alemán valora el cruce contra el Alavés de LaLiga
articles.summary: El técnico alemán valora el cruce contra el Alavés de LaLiga
articles.body: Hansi Flick analizó este sábado el encuentro de LaLiga contra el Alavés correspondiente a la jornada 11 y disputado en el Spotify Camp Nou. El Barça goleó al conjunto vasco y recuperó el liderato. Partido "Hemos parado al rival. Esperábamos que defendieran bien y corrieran en transición. Hemos controlado el partido y hemos estado centrados en defensa. Estoy contento por cómo hemos jugado, sobre todo en la primera mitad". De Jong "Tenemos que pensar de forma distinta porque tenemos a cuatro defensas fuera de juego, lesionado, que esperamos que vuelvan pronto. Pero no sabemos cuándo lo harán. Le pregunté a Frenkie si podía jugar de central, y dijo que sí, y lo valoro. Y Fariñas también jugó a gran nivel, de lateral, y se merecía este partido. Es muy profesional". Gavi "Tenemos que ir cambiando a los jugadores. Puedes pensar unos cambios, y luego el partido te lleva por otro lado, y la cosa cambia. Teníamos a Rodri, Frenkie, Fermín... había distintos cambios a hacer. Hay que aceptarlo". Lamine "Cuando marcas dos goles es más fácil salir. Había hablado con él en el descanso. Debe recuperar la confianza, en el uno contra uno... es importante que descanse. Ha sido un partido muy bueno por su parte. Es genial su nivel, y el de Fermín y Raphinha. Es lo que quería ver tras las derrotas. Nuestra reacción ha sido buena". Cien victorias "No suelo pensar en el pasado. Estoy muy contento por las cien victorias, seguro. Teníamos las esperanza de dirigir 100 partidos con el Barcelona y ahora son 100 ganados. El mejor tal vez sería la primera victoria en el Clásico, en Madrid... pero ha habido muchos. Ese triunfo me trae buenos recuerdos". Lesionados "No sabemos si se recuperarán esta semana. La evolución va bien, pero no están bien del todo. Hay que sobrevivir. Creo que Andreas está muy cerca de sumarse al equipo, pero hay que esperar. No correremos riesgos. Tras los dos partidos, hay luego descanso. Los necesitamos. No correremos riesgos". Brian Fariñas "Estoy muy contento con su actuación de hoy. Juega a buen nivel. Está bien conectado con Lamine, y eso es muy importante. Nos ha ayudado mucho. Merecía jugar. Es muy profesional. Está muy concentrado siempre". Pedri "Por los minutos y por la amarilla, lo hemos cambiado. Y era una oportunidad para Bernal. Era bueno para el equipo".

articles.title: Barcelona player ratings vs Deportivo Alaves: Lamine Yamal and Raphinha dazzle in dominant six-goal display
articles.summary: Barcelona bounced back from their Clasico defeat in emphatic fashion, as braces from Lamine Yamal and Raphinha powered a 6-1 win over Deportivo Alaves at the...
articles.body:
Barcelona bounced back from their Clasico defeat in emphatic fashion, as braces from Lamine Yamal and Raphinha powered a 6-1 win over Deportivo Alaves at the Spotify Camp Nou and sent Hansi Flick's side back to the top of La Liga.

The hosts were 4-0 up by half-time , with Fermin Lopez scoring once and setting up both of Raphinha's goals, before Yamal's VAR-approved chip and a fine finish from substitute Anthony Gordon stretched the lead further. Barcelona enjoyed 77 per cent possession and generated 3.19 expected goals (xG), and only a late Mariano Diaz strike spoiled the clean sheet, leaving them two points clear of Atletico Madrid on 30 points.

Joan Garcia - 7/10: Made two saves in the first half, denying Angel Perez at his near post and holding Carlos Protesoni's long-range effort, and punched clear with authority from a set-piece. Wrong-footed by Mariano's late strike.

Brian Farinas - 7/10: Handed a start at right-back in place of the injured Xavi Espart, he was tidy in possession and played his part in the slick move for Yamal's first goal.

Pau Cubarsi - 8/10: The key man in Barcelona's build-up, with 80 touches in the first half alone, and he headed away a dangerous Lucas Boye cross after De Jong had given the ball away.

Joao Cancelo - 7/10: Drifted infield to tee up Yamal for the fourth goal and was a constant outlet down the left. Booked for a clumsy foul on Perez on 57 minutes, before Alejandro Balde replaced him just after the hour.

Frenkie de Jong - 7/10: Deployed as a makeshift centre-back and largely comfortable in the role, though he carelessly gave the ball away in the 70th minute. Replaced by Gerard Martin eight minutes from time.

Rodri - 8/10: Controlled the tempo from the base of midfield and produced a perfectly weighted through ball for Gordon's goal, but his loose back pass let Mariano in for the Alaves consolation.

Pedri - 7/10: His through ball for Fermin started the move for the opener, and he was involved in the build-up to the fourth. Booked for dragging back Denis Suarez on 40 minutes and replaced by Marc Bernal at half-time.

Fermin Lopez - 9/10: A goal and two assists before half-time. Set up Raphinha for the opener and the third, and scored from an improbable angle on the right byline in between.

Lamine Yamal - 9/10: Assisted Fermin's goal, then hammered in a left-footed finish from the edge of the box for 4-0 and chipped Antonio Sivera for his second after VAR overturned an offside flag. Also had a first-time effort saved from close range. Replaced by Gordon on 74 minutes.

Karim Adeyemi - 7/10: Started ahead of Gordon on the left and troubled Nahuel Tenaglia with his pace, creating a chance for Yamal, but blazed over from close range when Fermin teed him up early in the second half.

Raphinha - 8/10: The captain tapped in Fermin's square ball for the opener and finished clinically for the third, taking his league tally to 15. Missed from close range when a hat-trick beckoned and was replaced by Gabriel Jesus on 62 minutes.

Marc Bernal - 7/10: Replaced Pedri at half-time and kept the midfield ticking over without fuss.

Alejandro Balde - 7/10: Came on for Cancelo on 62 minutes and combined well with Adeyemi and Fermin down the left.

Gabriel Jesus - 7/10: Needed just two minutes after coming on to slip Yamal through for the fifth goal, though he could not get on the end of a late scooped pass from Fermin.

Anthony Gordon - 8/10: Replaced Yamal on 74 minutes and capped his cameo with a cool lifted finish over Sivera from Rodri's through ball.

Gerard Martin - 6/10: Came on for De Jong on 82 minutes and was left behind by Mariano in the build-up to the Alaves goal.

Hansi Flick - 8/10: His three changes from the Clasico, including De Jong at centre-back and starts for Farinas and Adeyemi, paid off as his side responded to that setback in emphatic fashion.

articles.title: College football had its fun. Georgia is back to ruin everyone’s season
articles.summary: Georgia is angry, dominant and terrifying again. Its rout of Florida sent a blunt warning to everyone dreaming of a College Football Playoff run.
articles.body:
ATLANTA – Leave it to Georgia to ignore the chaos and carnage, and dutifully reset college football's October trip down the rabbit hole.

Excuse the most complete team in college football for that hiccup two weeks ago, that last-second giveaway to an Auburn team that just lost for the fourth time.

Use the 9-game schedule excuse, or whatever they do to make themselves feel better about losses in the big, bad SEC . None of that matters.

Georgia 's loud, undeniable statement in a 27-8 rout of Florida on Saturday is all you need to know about the head of the table in the College Football Playoff race .

There's the Boogeyman ― with the best roster and the best coach in college football — and there's everyone else.

Miami? The calendar has turned to November, and the ACC schedule is still the ACC schedule.

Ohio State? New quarterback, big problems.

Defending national champion Indiana? The magic, everyone, left with Fernando.

Unbeaten Utah and UCLA? Great stories, no business being on the same field with Georgia.

Then again, neither does any other team in the SEC, whose coaches constantly whine about depth and insular destruction, and how many of those teams could actually make a run in the CFP? If your answer includes Ole Miss or Texas, I'll remind you that Florida — which couldn't block Georgia, couldn't move the ball and was overwhelmed for 60 minutes — beat both of those teams.

Alabama is flawed, and could be looking for a new coach come December, after USC fires perpetual underachiever Lincoln Riley . Kentucky is raw and unproven, and not every SEC road game is Texas A&M, Oklahoma and South Carolina, fellas.

And for the love of Lane, please don't talk about LSU ― which has played two games of significance and lost both.

Two weeks ago, Florida beat Texas in Austin, found a starting quarterback and was surging. The Gators left Atlanta with another blowout loss, another year of searching for answers to the problem that won't go away.

The same problem the rest of college football now has to deal with over the second half of the season.

If there's one truism right now in college football, it's this: hell hath no fury like a ticked off and motivated Georgia. And Georgia with two weeks to prepare for a rivalry game? Forget it.

This is the beauty of Georgia coach Kirby Smart, who has won 10 of 11 in this series, and won them every way possible. Routes early on in the decade of dominance gave way to fourth-quarter saves, which then led to the statement game of this season.

The Georgia defense flexed, and Florida had no response. Four turnovers, and a run game that averaged less than three yards per carry with the best running back in the SEC (Jadan Baugh).

There were sacks and pressures and tackles for loss. There was pressure off the edge, and the interior pocket collapsing and coverage over the top in the secondary that eliminated any mistake.

A defensive clinic unlike anything we've seen from a Smart defense since the back-to-back national championships in 2021-22. Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis and Nakobe Dean aren't running around now, but there could be just as many NFL draft picks off this defense. They're just not household names yet.

There's junior edges Chris Cole, who returned another fumble for a touchdown, Justin Williams and Quintavius Johnson, and freshmen edge Khamari Brooks. And that's just part of a deep, and interchangeably devastating front seven.

And if we've seen anything in the past three seasons of Big Ten dominance in the national championship game, it's that defense dictates CFP runs. Michigan, Ohio State and Indiana all had elite defenses that set the tone in every playoff game.

So Georgia doesn't exactly have an elite offense, and can't stress defenses any number of ways with a variety of skill players. It doesn't need to.

Midway through the fourth quarter, with Florida trailing 24-0 in a game that seemed like 44-0, a Georgia turnover gave the Gators an opportunity to avoid their first shutout in this rivalry since 1982. Since a grown man named Herschel was running over everyone and everything.

It took an interference call in the end zone on fourth down to give Florida a shot at ending the shutout. Smart was furious with the call, and was still stalking the officials as Tramell Jones converted a short run for Florida's first points of the game.

Hell hath no fury like a ticked off Georgia.

Matt Hayes is the senior national college football writer for USA TODAY Sports Network. Follow him on X at @MattHayesCFB . Listen to him daily, from 12-2 p.m., on 1010XL-Jacksonville .

articles.title: Coventry, Ipswich, Hull - promoted trio enjoy positive starts
articles.summary: The three teams have collected a respectable 31 points in total after nine games, and all currently sit above the relegation zone.
articles.body:
It was only a few weeks ago that it seemed life in the Premier League might prove a step too far for newly promoted Coventry City.

After storming to the Championship title last season to secure their return to the top flight for the first time since 2001, Frank Lampard's side were given little time to settle into their new surroundings when the campaign began in August.

By the end of their first month back in the Premier League, Coventry were rooted to the bottom of the table, having lost all four of their matches by a combined score of 10-0.

The final defeat of that brutal introduction - a 5-0 hammering at the hands of high-flying Brighton - was enough to convince even the most optimistic supporters that a return to the Championship could be on the cards.

But since that humbling defeat on the south coast almost six weeks ago, Lampard's side have breathed new life into their campaign, winning three of their next five matches.

After back-to-back victories over Nottingham Forest and Newcastle United in September, Saturday's 3-1 win over Sunderland lifted the Sky Blues to 15th in the table.

Coventry are not the only newly promoted side to have impressed, with former Championship rivals Ipswich Town and Hull City also making encouraging starts.

The three teams have collected a combined 31 points after nine games, the 13th-highest tally by promoted sides at this stage in Premier League history.

Hull and Ipswich account for 22 of those points, with Sergej Jakirovic and Gary O'Neil's sides both sitting on 11.

Coventry are slightly behind their promoted peers, but the Sky Blues' three victories have still earned them a respectable nine points.

And there is further encouragement for the newcomers - since the 2010-11 season, all 18 promoted teams who have collected at least 11 points from their opening nine games have avoided relegation.

When reflecting on Coventry's summer spending spree, it is clear they were under no illusion of what it takes to compete in the Premier League.

The Sky Blues constructed major surgery on their playing squad by shelling out more than £140m on 12 permanent signings.

That splurge included the arrivals of Caleb Yirenkyi for a club-record fee, Carl Rushworth from Brighton, and Sidiki Cherif from Fenerbahce.

Lampard also added Premier League experience in the form of Loum Tchaouna from Burnley and Taiwo Awoniyi from Nottingham Forest.

After a summer of such upheaval in the West Midlands, it is no surprise it took Lampard a few weeks - five to be exact - to find his winning touch.

Hindsight has also been kind to Coventry. The fact three of their first four Premier League matches were against the current top three - Arsenal, Manchester City and Brighton - was clearly far from the ideal introduction.

After Saturday's 3-1 win over Sunderland, midfielder Jack Rudoni insisted his side still "believed" in their quality after a bruising start to the campaign.

"We always had that belief," Rudoni told BBC Sport. "We have a really good squad here, where the morale is good and we get behind each other, which is what we will continue to do all season.

"We know it's not going to be an easy ride, there's going to be ups and downs - but hopefully more ups than downs. Starting today with another three points, so we can build on that now."

'Our lads have some character and we just need to keep it up'

When Ipswich Town secured their return to the Premier League in May, few expected much from the Tractor Boys.

Their promotion to the top flight in 2024, ending a 22-year absence, exposed just how ill-equipped they were to compete at that level.

By the end of the 2024-25 season, Ipswich finished 19th, recording just four wins from 38 Premier League games.

But having secured an immediate return to the top flight, and after significant investment in the squad over the summer, the Tractor Boys look set to put up more of a fight this time around.

The Championship runners-up's summer business was headlined by the return of Julio Enciso, who spent part of the 2024-25 campaign on loan at Portman Road.

The Paraguay international has been instrumental in Ipswich's rise this season, assisting their opening goal against Sunderland before setting up another against Manchester United at Old Trafford the following week.

More recently, the 22-year-old has scored in consecutive matches against Nottingham Forest and Hull City, helping his side secure vital points against two teams who could be fighting for Premier League survival come the end of the season.

After Saturday's 2-2 draw with Hull, O'Neil praised his side's "character" after they fought from behind for the second Premier League match in a row.

"It's tough to be in control and find yourselves 2-1 down with the place bouncing," O'Neil told BBC Match of the Day.

"Our lads have some character and we just need to keep it up. Hull are a very good side and I'm really pleased with how we did against them."

Are Hull under pressure despite dream start?

The Premier League season had barely begun when Hull City made waves.

In their first match in the top flight since being relegated in 2017, the Tigers stunned Manchester United with a 2-0 victory on the opening weekend.

Although much of the attention centred on what the result meant for United manager Michael Carrick, Hull were quickly emerging as one of the season's feel-good stories.

Having earned promotion to the Premier League through the Championship play-offs, Jakirovic's side were flying the flag for the promoted clubs in the early weeks of the campaign.

After following up their opening-day triumph with a 1-0 win at Coventry, Hull earned respectable draws against Aston Villa and Chelsea.

But since suffering their first defeat of the season, the Tigers have collected just three points from their four matches since.

And with Arsenal and Brighton up next, the Tigers will know their impressive start could count for little if they fail to add to their points tally soon.

But the Premier League is a marathon, not a sprint - and all three promoted clubs will have belief that they can build on their encouraging starts.

articles.summary: El Elche, que lleva tres partidos sin encajar, busca mejorar sus datos de local • Aguirre trata de encontrar la reacción después de tres partidos
articles.body: Elche y Valencia se enfrentan en el Martínez Valero (18:30 horas) con objetivos y necesidades dispares, aunque con un objetivo similar: aumentar su productividad ofensiva. El equipo franjiverde es el que menos remates totales intenta como local de toda Primera división. Los blanquinegros son los visitantes que menos disparan. El Elche quiere liquidar su gran cuenta pendiente de la temporada: ganar en casa. Un triunfo permitiría al conjunto ilicitano consolidar su reacción y alejarse de la zona de descenso. El equipo de Martín Anselmi llega reforzado tras golear en Vallecas (0-3) y encadena cuatro jornadas sin perder, con ocho de los últimos doce puntos y tres porterías a cero consecutivas. Gran parte de su mejoría se explica por su notable rendimiento a domicilio. Ahora necesita trasladar esa solidez al Martínez Valero. Tras un calendario exigente, sólo ha sumado un punto de doce como local, logrado ante el Celta (0-0). En un duelo directo por la permanencia, busca abrir distancia con la zona roja. Anselmi mantiene la duda de Fer Niño por problemas lumbares. El Valencia sigue sin arrancar. Y esa es la peor noticia para un Javier Aguirre que no ha obrado el efecto revulsivo que se esperaba con su llegada. La derrota ante el Villarreal en la última jornada en el tiempo añadido sentó como una patada en la boca del estómago. Pero un punto arriba o abajo, el equipo sigue sin ser fiable ni en ataque ni en defensa y continúa en puestos de descenso con una sola victoria, que logró el interino Óscar Sánchez en Mendizorroza. El técnico mexicano ha sumado dos puntos en tres partidos desde que llegó al banquillo de Mestalla, aunque confía en que la reacción venga con la recuperación de jugadores lesionados. Lemar vs. Javi Guerra. El centrocampista francés es un fijo en los equipos titulares de Anselmi y su aportación se deja notar en los últimos partidos, aunque no brille tanto en funciones ofensivas. Por su parte, Javi Guerra no termina de romper como en otras temporadas, pero sigue siendo un jugador diferencial en la parte ofensiva, que es la que necesita mejorar Aguirre.

articles.title: Athletic - Real Sociedad: Que siga la fiesta
articles.standfirst: Los rojiblancos llegan lanzados tras golear al Getafe y los txuri-urdin encadenan cuatro triunfos ligueros seguidos
articles.summary: Los rojiblancos llegan lanzados tras golear al Getafe y los txuri-urdin encadenan cuatro triunfos ligueros seguidos
articles.body: El Athletic recibe este domingo a la Real Sociedad en San Mamés en un derbi al que llega con la confianza recuperada después de dos goleadas consecutivas. Los rojiblancos han marcado diez goles en apenas cinco días, tras superar al Getafe (4-0) en Liga y al AE Prat (1-6) en Copa. El equipo de Edin Terzic busca dar continuidad a su mejoría frente a un rival que acumula cuatro victorias consecutivas en Liga. Será el primer derbi oficial del técnico alemán, que ya se ha enfrentado a los donostiarras en la Euskal Herria Txapela, con triunfo rojiblanco por la mínima. Por su parte, la Real probablemente está en uno de los mejores momentos de su historia al visitar San Mamés, porque ha sumado seis victorias y un empate en las últimas ocho jornadas y porque ha enlazado cinco derbis sin perder, lo que hace que Pellegrino Matarazzo y sus futbolistas sean optimistas a la hora de pensar en alargar esas buenas rachas llevándose los tres puntos a casa, aunque el de Nueva Jersey ya avisó que el pasado poco cuenta en este tipo de partidos. Con respecto a los onces, el técnico de la Real, que viene realizando rotaciones, parece tener claro su equipo titular para esta noche, aunque desde fuera hay algunas dudas. Con Remiro en la portería, todo indica que Aramburu volverá a una defensa con los habituales Jon Martín, Sarr y Sergio Gómez. En el Athletic, Iñigo Ruiz de Galarreta será baja por una lesión muscular en los isquiotibiales. La buena noticia es el regreso de Oihan Sancet, que ha entrenado con normalidad durante la semana y está disponible como Peio Canales. Terzic ha destacado la importancia emocional del derbi y el alemán ha pedido a sus jugadores intensidad, pero también cabeza fría. Ha insistido en que lo importante es ganar, independientemente de sus buenos antecedentes ante Pellegrino Matarazzo. El encuentro tendrá además un componente simbólico con el homenaje al 50 aniversario de la histórica exhibición de la ikurriña protagonizada por Iribar y Kortabarria en Atotxa.

articles.title: Vinicius, dos años después del 'no Balón de Oro': los números de su caída
articles.standfirst: Se han cumplido dos años de su "lo haré diez veces" y las estadísticas dibujan un declive, con sus goles en Liga desplomados de 0,67 a 0,15 por 90 minutos
articles.summary: Se han cumplido dos años de su "lo haré diez veces" y las estadísticas dibujan un declive, con sus goles en Liga desplomados de 0,67 a 0,15 por 90 minutos
articles.body: Uno de los tweets más célebres del planeta fútbol ha cumplido dos años esta semana y continúa convertido en una vara de medir que su mismo autor plantó. “Eu farei 10 vezes se for preciso”: lo haré diez veces si hace falta. Lo escribió Vinicius, la noche del 28 de octubre de 2024, con el Balón de Oro camino de los brazos de Rodri y un desafío en boca. Prometía multiplicar, y los números, que no entienden de agravios ni de discursos, han tomado el camino contrario. El repaso periodo a periodo —el 'prime' en la 2023/24, el tramo posterior al Balón de Oro, la 2025/26 y la presente 2026/27— precisamente no describe una venganza, sino un desgaste que afecta a casi todas las facetas de su juego. Empecemos por el gol, su carta de presentación hacia el éxito. En su mejor momento —la 2023/24 y el arranque de la 2024/25, hasta aquel 28 de octubre— rondaba los 0,67 goles por noventa minutos en Liga y los 0,80 en Champions. Esta 2026/27 marca 0,15 en el campeonato y ni uno solo en Europa. La traducción en minutos por gol es demoledora: de 125 minutos para ver puerta en Liga a 585, casi seis partidos y medio esperando un tanto que antes caía cada hora y poco. Y lo mismo cuenta la suma de goles más asistencias, su contribución total al marcador: de 1,04 por noventa en su mejor Liga a 0,62 ahora, de 1,00 en Champions a cero esta temporada. La caída no fue un desplome súbito, sino una pendiente, y el primer escalón llegó justo tras la gala. En el tramo final de la 2024/25 sus goles en Liga bajaron de 0,67 a 0,36 y en Champions de 0,80 a 0,56. Lo llamativo es que su generación de ocasiones apenas se resintió: el xG se movió de 0,49 a 0,43 en Liga, y las grandes ocasiones que disfrutó pasaron de 1,04 a 0,72 por noventa. Seguía llegando; empezaba a fallar lo que antes resolvía. El regate en Europa, en cambio, se le apagó de golpe: de encarar 8,33 veces por noventa a 5,75, de completar 3,69 a 1,82. La herida del Balón de Oro, dijeran lo que dijeran sus palabras, dejó marca en su desborde. La 2025/26 ofreció un espejismo de recuperación, y conviene decirlo para ser justo. Vinicius sostuvo una versión digna en Liga: 0,51 goles por noventa, una precisión de tiro del 61,3% —la más alta de todo el recorrido—, 0,67 de goles más asistencias y una cifra de balones perdidos que bajó a 16,28, señal de un juego algo más ordenado. En Champions el cuadro fue más contradictorio: su xG trepó hasta 0,62, el mejor de todos los periodos, y sus grandes ocasiones subieron a 1,15 por noventa, pero el gol se le resistía (0,38) y falló 0,92 de esas ocasiones claras, su peor registro en ese apartado. Generaba más que nunca en Europa y transformaba menos. El problema dejaba de estar en la producción para instalarse en el remate. La 2026/27 ha ratificado el temor de muchos madridistas. En Liga, además de esos 0,15 goles, su precisión de tiro se ha hundido hasta el 38,9%, con diferencia la peor de las cuatro etapas, y los regates completados han caído a 2,15 por noventa desde los 2,78 del 'prime'. En Champions, la competición que reinó hace años, el diagnóstico es aún más severo: cero goles, un xG testimonial de 0,10, ni una sola gran ocasión generada y apenas 2,08 regates intentados, cuando en su mejor momento encaraba más de ocho veces por partido. Los toques en el área rival, eso sí, se mantienen altos (10,46 en Liga, por encima incluso del prime): pisa la zona de peligro con la misma insistencia de siempre, pero no con el mismo veneno. Hay un dato que, mal leído, parecería una mejora: pierde menos balones que nunca, 14,92 por noventa en Liga frente a los 18,64 del prime, y 11,25 en Champions frente a 18,30. Cualquier entrenador firmaría esa cifra en un centrocampista. En un extremo desequilibrante, en cambio, no habla de madurez sino de renuncia. Arriesga menos porque intenta menos. El Vinicius que perdía veinte pelotas por partido era el mismo que volvía loca a una defensa entera; el que las cuida es también el que ya no asusta. Dos años después de aquel “lo haré diez veces”, la cuenta del desafío se ha invertido: donde prometió multiplicar, ha dividido. Y sin embargo, conviene no firmar el acta de defunción. El xG casi intacto en Liga —0,47 esta temporada, prácticamente el del prime— y los toques en el área, que no bajan, sostienen algo de esperanza: Vinicius sigue llegando a los mismos sitios. No ha perdido el camino hasta el área ni la posición del verdugo; ha perdido el último movimiento, ese disparo que ahora se marcha fuera dos de cada tres veces. Le falta, nada más y nada menos, volver a acertar. El escalafón del Balón de Oro ha ido tomando nota de todo esto con frialdad para el brasileño. En 2024 Vinicius acabó segundo, un podio que buena parte del mundo del fútbol sintió como injusto y que él mismo convirtió en bandera. Doce meses después cayó al 16º puesto, y en la última edición se ha quedado en el 17º. La votación, que premia títulos y rendimiento individual, no hace sino reflejar lo que dicen sus registros y su peso menguante en el Madrid. Le espera, por tanto, la cuesta más empinada, y le toca subirla a plena luz. Por dignidad, porque la palabra dada envejece mal cuando los goles no acompañan. Y por el club, que en lugar de soltarle la mano se la apretó: lo renovó hasta 2032 cuando los números pedían prudencia, y esa firma es confianza y deuda a la vez.

articles.title: Manchester United: Are Old Trafford club really heading for a relegation scrap?
articles.summary: Manchester United's current tally of nine points from seven games would not even get them 30 points if it was continued for the full season.
articles.body:
"We've got to keep moving forward and winning games, simple as that," said Michael Carrick in that considered way of his, after their 2-0 defeat by Chelsea on Saturday .

Carrick did get relegated once, with West Ham at the start of his playing career.

The Hammers were supposed to be too good to go down in 2002-03. Aside from Carrick, they had England goalkeeper David James in their squad. Joe Cole, Jermain Defoe and Trevor Sinclair all played more than 40 games in all competitions.

But down they went, finishing third bottom with 42 points. It remains the highest tally any side has been relegated with across a 38-game Premier League campaign.

To put that into context, Manchester United's current tally of seven points from nine games would not even get them 30 points if it was continued for the full season.

So, are United really destined for a relegation scrap?

You would have to be touching 60 to have any recollection of the last time United were relegated.

Legend has it that old boy Denis Law sent them down with an impudent back heel he didn't celebrate when he was at Manchester City. The reality is United were already doomed under then-boss Tommy Docherty.

United have not been in the relegation zone after nine games or more since November 1986, when they collected a single point in Sir Alex Ferguson's first two games in charge following Ron Atkinson's dismissal.

Their lowest position after at least nine games of a season since then was 17th in 1989-90. They are back there again right now, mainly thanks to the failings of others in results elsewhere on Saturday.

It is now nine games in all competitions since Carrick's side won, their worst run since 1988-89. Their single Premier League win of the season was when they came from behind to beat Ipswich at home in August.

Of course, United's supporters have very recent experience of seeing their team in the lower reaches of the table. They were 16th under Ruben Amorim after 37 games of the 2024-25 season. The caveat is they were 14 points clear of third-bottom Leicester and at no point in that tortuous campaign were they in danger of relegation.

One club that has been at real risk in recent years is Tottenham, who were third bottom and two points behind West Ham with four games of last season remaining.

So, it could happen, even if it remains unlikely a club that should post revenues in excess of £700m for the current campaign will finish in the bottom three.

"You can look at it like that, or you can look at how far you can move up the league quite quickly if you win football matches," was Carrick's response when asked if his players are equipped for the "mentality shift" required to deal with the present situation. "That's the way it's got to be approached."

Martinez's 'inexplicable' 83 seconds cost Man Utd and Carrick

Rogers shines, 3/10 for sent-off Martinez - player ratings for Chelsea v Man Utd

Chelsea beat 10-man Man Utd to heap further pressure on Carrick

Yet, as Carrick said, in order to save themselves, United need to win matches.

Their next game is against Aston Villa at Old Trafford on 8 November. Among the seven matches they have after that are trips to Liverpool, Newcastle and Arsenal.

As yet, there is no word about Carrick's future, although before Saturday's loss, the expectation was he would be in charge for Tuesday's Champions League encounter with Roma.

But these are unchartered waters and no-one can be absolutely sure what happens next. It is clear that many players need to improve their performance levels.

United will be without one of those players, Lisandro Martinez, who will miss the Villa game due to suspension after his red card at Chelsea, which was branded "inexplicable" by former World Cup final official Darren Cann on BBC Sport.

Martinez's longer-term future with the club is uncertain, but clearly he could not leave until January at the earliest.

His contract expires in the summer, and the Argentine's patchy injury record had already raised questions over whether it was worth triggering the clause that would commit United to another season.

What is financial implication of relegation?

After just nine games, it is a bit early to dig into the actual consequences of relegation for United, but the numbers might offer pause for thought.

In May, respected football finance blogger Paul Quinn, known as The Esk, calculated that Tottenham's "absolute revenue loss" , external would be between £197m-£235m if they did go down.

As one of the league's highest recipients of TV income, United would not remotely be covered by the parachute payments available to relegated clubs.

It seems unlikely that many, if any, of their squad would have relegation clauses, and while United have huge commercial income, it is not known to what extent that would be affected by clauses triggered by relegation.

United also have £1.15bn worth of debt, made up of bonds that were renegotiated in June at a higher interest rate, a revolving credit facility and outstanding transfer fee payments.

The club are also about to launch a fan consultation before coming up with final plans for a new stadium, which are due to be submitted either in late 2027 or early 2028.

United fans once again chanted their opposition to a new stadium at Stamford Bridge during the Chelsea defeat.

It is a complicated picture, and even though it seems highly unlikely that the doomsday scenario will become reality, the mere fact that United are in the position they are underlines just how poor their form has been.

articles.title: B/R's 2026 College Football Winners and Losers from Week 9
articles.summary: The Halloween version of college football Saturday offered its fair share of treats despite a slim slate on paper with just two matchups between ranked teams.
articles.body:
The Halloween version of college football Saturday offered its fair share of treats despite a slim slate on paper with just two matchups between ranked teams.

In those, Texas Tech broke free late to keep its head afloat in the Big 12 over conference foe Arizona, and Georgia walloped rival Florida as the showdown formerly dubbed the "World's Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party" moved inside and north to Atlanta for a year.

SMU faltered to see its playoff hopes disintegrate, while the national champion Hoosiers needed some heroics and a 60-yard field goal to stay in the mix and keep Minnesota haunting their hopes at bay.

Top-ranked Miami, Utah and UCLA remained unbeaten, but Ohio State's offense minus injured quarterback Julian Sayin was a wet blanket in a rainy loss to USC in The Coliseum.

It was an eventful day, even without the marquee matchups. Here are your winners and losers from Week 9.

Joey McGuire's Texas Tech Red Raiders expected to compete for a national championship this year with a transfer quarterback at the helm.

They still may – it just won't be the one they expected.

After Brendan Sorsby transferred from Cincinnati, he was ruled ineligible after getting caught up in a gambling scandal, leading the Red Raiders to start Will Hammond under center. Following an awful loss to Cincinnati last week, McGuire made a change to Thomas Castellanos.

The fifth-year senior on his fourth school was dynamic in a top-25 showdown against Arizona, helping his team erase a 10-point first-half deficit and win a 34-26 showdown that is pivotal to their Big 12 and playoff hopes.

Castellanos was the catalyst with Red Raider resurgence, throwing for 144 yards and a pair of touchdowns. But his biggest boost came on the ground where he ran for 117 yards and a score, kick-starting an incredible showing by TTU's rushing attack.

They added 175 yards from J'Koby Williams on their way to a 328-yard rushing performance that grabbed them a pivotal conference win and helped them overcome Noah Fifita's 417-yard passing outburst.

Loser: Minnesota's Shot to Party Like 1956

Indiana doesn't look like a national championship team so far this season, but the Hoosiers just keep winning like one.

On Saturday, they somehow survived in overtime 23-16 against Minnesota despite a barrage of miscues. The Golden Gophers did enough to beat back-to-back ranked teams for the first time since 1956, but they just couldn't halt heroics.

After Luke Drzewiecki's 60-yard field goal put the Gophers ahead by three with 19 seconds to go, Grant Wilson hit two chunk plays to gain 33 yards and give Hoosiers long-range kicker Paddy McAteer his own 60-yard attempt, which he drilled at the buzzer.

It took IU one play to score in overtime, and the defense stopped Minnesota to secure the win.

"This is entertainment, so we thought we'd put some entertainment value into this game," IU coach Curt Cignetti told CBS after the game. "It was really like, 'How many things you could do wrong?'"

This year's version of Indiana is doing very un-Cignetti-like things. Saturday, they shanked a field goal, got another one blocked, botched the snap on a field goal and shanked a pair of punts that led to 10 Gophers points.

Still, somehow, they found a way in a game where starting quarterback Josh Hoover got dinged up, pulled and the backup quarterback led them to the win. The Hoosiers are still in position to make the playoffs, and Minnesota is left hurting after somehow letting it slip away.

In an imperfect year without a clear national title favorite, the top-ranked Miami Hurricanes just continue to churn out battle-tested wins.

Last year's national runners-up haven't had the explosiveness of Utah, and they aren't the feel-good story that UCLA is, but they've got without question the highest ceiling of the three remaining unbeatens, and they are getting some ulcer-inducing moments, too.

A couple of weeks ago, they needed overtime to beat an outmanned rival Florida State team. Then Saturday, they squeaked out a sweaty 38-35 win over a North Carolina team that punched back time and time again.

Late in the fourth quarter following a go-ahead Miami scoring drive, Marquise Lightfoot sacked Tar Heels quarterback Billy Edwards, forcing a fumble that was recovered by Justin Scott. The 'Canes capitalized with a touchdown three plays later to take a 10-point lead and provide wiggle room.

UNC marched right back with a touchdown, recovered two onside kicks – both of which were overturned due to Tar Heels penalties (offsides and an illegal block) – and failed to recover a third as Miami ran out the clock.

The win sets up next week's premiere matchup with No. 5-ranked Notre Dame in the latest in a long line of massive games this college football season has brought us.

Say what you want about UCLA's lack of style points, but the Bruins just keep on churning out Ws.

Saturday was never supposed to be a challenge with a home game against Nevada and a break from the grueling Big Ten schedule, but coach Bob Chesney's team still dominated the Wolfpack in a game that was never close.

The final score wound up being 27-0, but the Bruins were dominant, and the defense that has won them so many games this season was brilliant once again, keeping Nevada in check with just 176 total yards and 10 first downs.

Backup quarterback Ty Dieffenbach – who was thrust into the lineup with Nico Iamaleava's season-ending injury a few weeks ago – wasn't great, but he just keeps on being a steady field manager. He finished with 178 passing yards, a throwing score and a rushing score in the win.

Next week's road trip to Minnesota is intriguing, but UCLA's remaining schedule is navigable with Illinois, Michigan, USC joining the Gophers on the schedule. Chesney's team is one of three unbeatens and even has wiggle room for a loss.

With Jacksonville's EverBank Stadium undergoing a massive renovation this year, the Georgia-Florida game – for years known as the World's Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party – moved indoors this year to Atlanta's Mercedes-Benz Stadium.

Maybe Florida's offense took too long to realize where the game was. The Gators struggled to get started, and even though the Bulldogs offense sputtered along once again, they had no issues in a 27-8 win.

The reasons were largely the things that have hamstrung first-year coach Jon Sumrall's team when it has been at its worst this year.

First, the Gators failed to get consistent quarterback play as starter Aaron Philo threw a pair of early interceptions. When he was yanked in favor of Tramell Jones Jr., he started strong but dropped a sack-fumble picked up by UGA linebacker Chris Cole and returned 66 yards for a touchdown.

Despite some third-down struggles and offensive inconsistency, Gunner Stockton and the Dawgs held a 24-0 halftime lead and never looked back. The 17th-ranked Gators never got its running game going, either, with just 48 total yards on the ground.

It was far from the rivalry renewal Gators fans hoped for.

With Cincinnati hosting sixth-ranked Utah at Nippert Stadium on Saturday, the Bearcats had a shot at knocking off consecutive Big 12 opponents at home after last week's win over Texas Tech.

Instead, the Utes continued flashing that championship swag with a sterling start on their way to a dominant 49-25 win over the five-win Bearcats.

Cincinnati is a good team, and Utah just dismantled them, as Morgan Scalley's Utes remained one of just three unbeaten Football Bowl Subdivision teams.

Not only did the Utes offense pile up four first-half touchdowns, the defense rose to the occasion, too, in a near-perfect first half.

First, they held the Bearcats to a missed field goal in a red-zone opportunity, then they forced another field goal late in the first half to keep Cincy from building any momentum heading into halftime. They also got a 51-yard Rabbit Evans scoop-and-score to build the lead and a pick-six to close the half on their way to a 42-point first-half outburst. Things got sloppy in the second half, but it was still an easy win that included 534 yards and 27 first downs.

On top of that, Devon Dampier was nearly perfect, and the rushing attack cruised as well as the Utes had zero issues remaining undefeated and staying in the driver's seat in the Big 12.

Talk about an off-the-radar loss on an expectedly quiet college football Saturday without a lot of top-shelf matchups. The SMU Mustangs delivered a stunner. Or maybe "didn't deliver," is a better description.

The 19th-ranked Mustangs headed to sleepy Syracuse, got down early, retook the lead, then allowed an 11-play, 68-yard Orange scoring drive with 18 seconds left to lose 30-27.

Steve Angeli went 7-for-8 on the drive, leading Syracuse to another win after shocking North Carolina last week. For SMU, though, the loss has season-long ramifications. Now, not only do the Mustangs face an uphill battle to compete for the ACC title, the College Football Playoff hopes dwindle to a glimmer.

Again, offensive balance was the biggest issue for Rhett Lashlee's team. While star quarterback Kevin Jennings was scintillating, a Mustangs rushing attack that entered the game 66th nationally mustered just 70 yards.

Syracuse kept things close, then Angeli steadily surged the Orange downfield for a monster upset.

Maybe Notre Dame was looking ahead to next week's crucial game against Miami. Maybe the Fighting Irish simply weren't ready to play, even coming off a bye following the heartbreaking loss at BYU.

Whatever the case, they clung to just a one-point halftime lead over two-win Navy at Gillette Stadium in Foxboro, Massachusetts. Then, they suddenly came to life.

After the break, CJ Carr got the passing game going, and the Irish went on a 21-point barrage to wind up running away from the overmatched Midshipmen with a 35-13 win. This was the Notre Dame team everybody expected to see rather than the one that simply had sleepwalked through the past six quarters.

Defensively, they seemed to catch on to defending the option and got going, too. Whether or not the Irish regained enough of themselves to feel confident heading into next week's top-five showdown against the top-ranked Hurricanes, we'll see soon.

But the Irish are definitely clicking more than they were following a stellar second-half showing.

For a while, it appeared Northwestern was going to seize its opportunity to continue deep into the season's second half with an opportunity to make the College Football Playoff.

All that disappeared in multiple quick flicks of Dylan Raiola's arm as Oregon's backup quarterback erased a 14-point Wildcats lead with a flurry of terrific passes as the Ducks offense finally took flight in a 34-26 win.

Raiola punctuated a 21-point second-half outburst with a 75-yard scoring strike to Dakorien Moore, erasing Northwestern's hopes to continue rising in the rankings. The 20th-rated Wildcats have experienced a terrific season, but it won't be special.

The pass defense is the culprit, allowing Raiola to throw for 336 yards and a trio of scores where the Ducks had really been struggling.

Even so, the Wildcats are a program on the rise. In a year where they opened a sparkling new stadium, enjoyed a resurgence with coordinator Chip Kelly calling plays for quarterback Aidan Chiles and turning into a tough out for everybody, Northwestern is a terrific story.

But the Ducks ripped out pages of any storybook finish Saturday.

We've already mentioned one former Washington State coach for all the work he's done at Wake Forest with Jake Dickert making national waves. But another former Cougar head coach is doing some major under-the-radar work, too.

That would be Jimmy Rogers, who in his first year at Iowa State faced a ridiculous roster hurdle as only 44 Cyclones returned from last year's team. Many of those former players followed last year's coach, Matt Campbell, to Penn State.

Even with the overhaul, though, Rogers has Iowa State at 4-4 after Saturday night's wild-and-wacky 51-49 home upset of No. 24 Oklahoma State in Ames. The crowd was crazy, the stadium was rocking and Jaylen Raynor, Aiden Flora and Co. led a high-octane offense to a huge win.

After Kyle Konrardy's game-winning 34-yard field goal, the crowd stormed the field and celebrated with their team of unheralded playmakers.

Raynor has been a weapon as a senior transfer from Arkansas State, and he enjoyed one of his best games with 357 total yards and four touchdowns against the Cowboys. Flora – a former walk-on – piled up 227 rushing yards, too.

You won't hear much about the Cyclones this year, and it's going to be an uphill battle to make a bowl game, but what Rogers has done in Year 1 piecemealing a roster that includes all 22 new starters is pretty incredible.

The Cyclones are a tough out every week, and that's saying a lot for the coaching job he's done.

Most times when a team loses its starting quarterback in the transfer portal era, the season's trajectory changes dramatically.

Ohio State is finding out the hard way what Oregon already knows after Julian Sayin's serious arm/shoulder injury suffered in the win over Indiana. In true freshman Luke Fahey's return to California for his first collegiate start, the Buckeyes couldn't muster any offense in a 30-18 loss to USC.

The Trojans were a completely different team than the one that played dead a week ago in a loss to Wisconsin, and defensive coordinator Gary Patterson called his best game in the win. But it was obvious Ohio State's simply wasn't the same juggernaut offense without Sayin leading it.

For one thing, megastar receiver Jeremiah Smith was rendered a spectator for much of the game with Fahey's inability to get him the ball. There were several notable Buckeyes drops, but the passing game simply was a nonfactor throughout the game.

For USC coach Lincoln Riley, it was a much-needed win to alleviate some of the pressure on him, even if this wasn't the same team that entered the game a national title contender. Once the whistle blew, it was clear the Buckeyes are no longer a threat.

Jake Dickert is the biggest rising coaching star nobody is talking about.

And Wake Forest just quietly continues to run roughshod through the season with a 13-point loss to top-ranked Miami the only blemish on an otherwise-spotless record that has them ranked 14th and climbing.

Saturday's complete-game, 51-7 wipe-out of Virginia was the latest speedbump in an ACC romp, and it just may have been the Demon Deacons' best showing of the season. Winston-Salem is rocking, and you'd better begin to pay attention.

Wake Forest scored on its first nine possessions until punting late in the fourth quarter of the laugher, but it wasn't just quarterback Gio Lopez and the offense that was brilliant.

The Demon Deacons played lights-out defense throughout, and Kam Sparks added a pair of punt returns for 94 yards to set up two of the scores, as well.

This Wake team is very good, and that shouldn't be a surprise with Dickert leading the way. After Dave Clawson stepped down, Wake grabbed Washington State's head coach, and he promptly won nine games last year. With Lopez in the fold, he's got a field general who can distribute the ball everywhere.

Colton Joseph has experienced his ups and downs leading Wisconsin's offense in his first year as the Badgers starting quarterback. Saturday, it did not go well for him or his team on either side of the ball.

The former Old Dominion signal-caller accounted for just 96 total yards and a fumble and was pulled from the game in favor of backup Ryan Hopkins. He didn't do any better as Iowa got off to a fast start and never looked back, smothering coach Luke Fickell's team in a 30-0 Hawkeyes victory in Iowa City.

Iowa made sure rival Wisconsin would build no momentum after it was ranked for the first time since Week 2 of the 2023 season. Total Hawkeyes domination took care of that.

The good news for the Badgers and hot-seat coach Fickell is the remaining schedule is navigable with Rutgers, Maryland, Purdue and Minnesota remaining and already five wins on the ledger.

But this was the opportunity for the Badgers to reannounce their place in the Big Ten hierarchy, a rugged road game a week after handling USC 24-7 in Camp Randall. Instead, it never really was close.

Maryland has to feel pretty badly after leading much of the game but falling in a last-second home loss by three to Illinois.

Out of the three Power Four programs who let go of their head coaches this week, the Terrapins were the only ones that didn't come out victorious, despite looking better than they have all year.

Baylor and North Carolina State – which parted ways with Dave Aranda and Dave Doeren, respectively – cruised to lopsided victories.

The Bears got things started under interim coach Joe Klanderman on Friday night by whipping a UCF team coming off a win over BYU in Orlando. The Bears treated their trip to Central Florida like a Disney World vacation, getting 319 yards and four touchdowns from DJ Lagway in a 41-9 win.

The Wolfpack handled Cal without issue, trouncing the Bears 31-10.

The Bears are now 5-3, and the Wolfpack moved to 4-4 with the victories. Maybe all they needed was a change in leadership? The coming weeks will tell us.

A week and a half ago, then-unbeaten James Madison was in the driver's seat for the Group of Six College Football Playoff spot until losing in overtime at Appalachian State.

Thursday, the Dukes' wheels came off against Troy at home in yet another overtime loss that knocked them out of the playoff picture altogether. JMU coach Billy Napier deserves ample blame for the 24-21 setback with a clock management gaffe for the ages.

The Dukes seemed to be cruising toward a game-winning field-goal attempt in regulation, sitting pretty with a 1st-and-10 from the Troy 37 with 31 seconds left and two timeouts. They proceeded to go 1-yard run, timeout, back-to-back negative rushes, timeout, incomplete pass, Hail Mary, overtime.

In OT, Napier eschewed a chip-shot field goal after getting the ball first, electing to go for it and falling short. When the Trojans got the ball back, their own short field goal won the game.

It was just a colossal coaching blunder that will take Napier from a Harrisonburg honeymoon to heartburn. The Dukes deserve plenty of blame for not playing well, but their coach flubbed up the ending.

articles.title: CFB Playoff Picture, Standings and Bracket Predictions After Week 9 of 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: The Ohio State Buckeyes became the latest top-five team to be upset during the 2026 college football season.
articles.body:
The Ohio State Buckeyes became the latest top-five team to be upset during the 2026 college football season.

Ohio State fell on the road at the USC Trojans in its first game with backup quarterback Luke Fahey at the helm in place of the injured Julian Sayin.

The Buckeyes will drop from the No. 2 spot in the AP Top 25, which will pave the way for the Georgia Bulldogs to jump back up to No. 2. UGA walloped the Florida Gators on Saturday afternoon.

The top-ranked Miami Hurricanes faced another battle in ACC play, but they survived a road trip to North Carolina to remain undefeated.

The Indiana Hoosiers almost suffered the same fate as Ohio State, but they found a way to beat the Minnesota Golden Gophers in overtime to avoid a second loss.

The CFP Playoff projections are based on results and rankings after Week 9's games.

Ohio State's first game with Luke Fahey at quarterback resulted in a road loss to USC.

USC opened up a 14-3 lead by the end of the first quarter and didn't let go of the lead against the No. 2 team in the country.

The Buckeyes all of a sudden have two losses and won't have their starting quarterback, Julian Sayin, to dig them out of the hole because of his injury.

Ohio State will tumble in Sunday's rankings, but it will still be in playoff range.

The Buckeyes' margin for error is now slim with losses to USC and the Texas Longhorns on their resume.

Ohio State's clash with the Oregon Ducks next week has less buzz than it did at the start of the season, and that's probably a good thing for the Buckeyes.

Ryan Day's team can still run the table in November to get to the Big Ten Championship Game, but if it suffers one more loss, there will be serious questions about its playoff prospects.

The Indiana Hoosiers survived an upset bid at home against the Minnesota Golden Gophers.

Curt Cignetti's team won in the first overtime period to move to 8-1 and remain in the race for the top four seeds.

Indiana now has three games left in the regular season to finish out at 11-1 and make the Big Ten Championship Game.

The Hoosiers are at home for two games in November and then go on the road to face the Washington Huskies. All three of those games are winnable, especially with the defense the Hoosiers have.

A one-loss Indiana team should, at minimum, be in contention for a first-round bye. It'll be in even better shape if it ends up as the Big Ten champion.

Texas Tech, BYU Bounce Back After Losses

Texas Tech and BYU both bounced back with wins on Saturday.

The Red Raiders won one of Saturday's two Top 25 clashes against the Arizona Wildcats.

Texas Tech utilized a quarterback switch with Thomas Castellanos taking over for Will Hammond.

At No. 13, Texas Tech is well positioned to be in the playoff field if it wins out. The Oklahoma State Cowboys are the only ranked team left on Tech's regular season schedule.

BYU rebounded from its loss to the UCF Knights with a home win over the Arizona State Sun Devils.

BYU's playoff hopes could come down to the Holy War against the Utah Utes next Saturday . Utah is the lone remaining unbeaten team in the Big 12.

If BYU beats Utah, the Big 12's chances of getting three teams into the playoff will increase.

articles.title: East Carolina freshman sustains fractured fibula from accidental slide tackle by ref
articles.summary: David Coleman Jr. sustained one of the most unfortunate injuries of the season.
articles.body:
One of the most unfortunate injuries of the college football season arrived Saturday during East Carolina's game against Temple.

Following a play in the second quarter, an official slipped and fell directly into the legs of East Carolina defensive back David Coleman Jr. The freshman had to be helped off the field with no weight on his right leg.

The official appeared to be trying to run through a group of ECU players and took a route around Coleman, but Coleman didn't see him and accidentally moved into his path. The ref didn't appear hurt on the play and immediately checked to see if Coleman was OK.

East Carolina went on to beat Temple 17-9. After the game, ECU head coach Blake Harrell revealed to reporters that an X-ray showed a fractured fibula for Coleman. He also affirmed the injury was an accident, while noting some larger issues with the officiating during the game:

"DC Coleman was taking the field there in the first half after a kick return. The official was coming down, making sure two guys heard the whistle, make sure they separated because sometimes those guys don't hear the whistle. "As he's coming down, he slips, falls into DC Coleman. DC got an X-ray at halftime, fractured his fibula there. Our thoughts and prayers are with him. That's just one of those things, kind of wild it happens. I've never seen that from an official — a few things happen in the ballgame that I've never seen — and unfortunate for DC."

"DC Coleman was taking the field there in the first half after a kick return. The official was coming down, making sure two guys heard the whistle, make sure they separated because sometimes those guys don't hear the whistle.

"As he's coming down, he slips, falls into DC Coleman. DC got an X-ray at halftime, fractured his fibula there. Our thoughts and prayers are with him. That's just one of those things, kind of wild it happens. I've never seen that from an official — a few things happen in the ballgame that I've never seen — and unfortunate for DC."

Coleman is a true freshman and was rated as a three-star recruit by Rivals . The Georgia native was ranked among the higher players in the Pirates' Class of 2026 . Per ECU's website , the Temple game was his fourth appearance of the season.

articles.summary: Tras el susto de la Copa, los azulones buscan refugio en el Coliseum
articles.body: El Getafe recibe este mediodía (14.00 horas) al Sevilla en un contexto de tensión agravada por el partido de Copa del Rey frente a la Lebrijana. Los azulones se aferran al Coliseum, donde no conocen la derrota en LaLiga este curso. García Plaza le ha devuelto la sonrisa a los sevillistas. Los andaluces intentarán aprovechar ese escenario para dar otro paso adelante. Llegan a la cita más relajados, cómodamente posicionados en la tabla. Además pasó sin apuros su eliminatoria en el torneo del KO frente al Sporting de Hortaleza. Cómo llega el Getafe: El Getafe recibe al Sevilla en un duelo clave para los del sur de Madrid. El equipo de Bordalás llega tras un agónico pase en Copa del Rey frente a la Lebrijana y dos goleadas en contra frente al Lugano en la Conference y Athletic en San Mamés. El cuadro azulón afronta el encuentro con las bajas de Mario Martín, expulsado en Bilbao, y Mojica por sanción, aunque recupera a Mangala para LaLiga después de su regreso en Copa por la puerta grande salvando los muebles de su equipo. Cómo llega el Sevilla: Los de García Plaza buscarán su segunda victoria consecutiva en LaLiga tras imponerse (2-0) a Osasuna en el Sánchez-Pizjuán. La balanza se inclina a favor del Sevilla en los enfrentamientos recientes entre ambos equipos. Ha ganado tres de los cinco últimos duelos de la competición casera, frente a una victoria del Getafe y un empate. El conjunto nervionense superó sin apuros su eliminatoria copera frente al Sporting de Hortaleza con la unidad B. Hoy volverán los actores principales: Odysseas, Agoumé, Fofana, Kike Salas, Suazo... La pasada campaña, Sow decidió el enfrentamiento con un tanto en la segunda mitad. Lo principal, según ha matizado el propio Bordalás, es frenar la sangría de goles en contra para volver a ver a un Getafe reconocible. El duelo del partido: Terrats vs Agoumé. El centrocampista catalán es uno de los jugadores predilectos de Bordalás. Polivalente, su mejor virtud es la capacidad para aparecer desde segunda línea. Ha pasado de ser una apuesta de futuro a convertirse en el termómetro de su equipo. Su sociedad con Fofana le hace crecer. La predicción de... Rocío Guevara: El ambiente enrarecido que rodea al Getafe puede jugar en contra, si bien es cierto que su única fortaleza este curso es el Coliseum. Pero el Sevilla está con la moral por las nubes y da guerra. GETAFE 1-2 SEVILLA
